name: Category Commander
author: 菅原隆志

sections.description:
Category Commander helps administrators organize WordPress categories, tags, and supported public custom taxonomies. It combines drag-and-drop ordering, restore history, health checks, guided category organization, CSV backups, click insights, and optional AI suggestions.

The beginner-friendly How to Use screen explains each feature and links directly to the correct page. Every plugin page starts by explaining its purpose, what will and will not change, and the three main steps. Pages are grouped into Basic tasks, Useful tools, and AI features so beginners can find the right screen without learning technical WordPress terms first. Category Organizer previews affected posts, primary categories, hierarchy, archive URLs, and permalink risks before moving all or selected posts, changing a parent, or changing a name or URL. A restore point is saved before applying. Category Organizer does not delete categories: a source category remains in place even when all of its posts are moved. Deleting unused categories is a separate action that requires selection and confirmation.

Main features

  • Category, tag, and public custom-taxonomy ordering
  • Saved order presets, history, restore, CSV, JSON, shortcode, PHP helpers, and REST support
  • Taxonomy Health Dashboard with prioritized local checks
  • Category Organizer for combining categories, moving selected posts, changing parents, and changing names or URLs, with impact preview and restore history
  • Primary category controls compatible with active Yoast SEO and Rank Math installations
  • Optional, non-blocking-by-default category, tag, hierarchy, and new-term rules
  • Optional local aggregate Category Click Insights
  • Optional OpenAI suggestions for taxonomy planning and post-editor category and tag selection
  • Existing-first suggestions and confirmation before creating or applying anything
  • API-free prompt copy for ChatGPT and other browser AI services
  • Editable prompts, reset buttons, and current GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna model choices

Privacy and external services

AI and Insights are disabled by default. No data is sent to OpenAI automatically. An API request occurs only after an authorized user enables AI and clicks a generation button. A post-editor request may include the current title and body, selected and existing categories and tags, and configured site summaries. Taxonomy planning may include the previewed taxonomy and optional aggregate Insights context. Visitor data, comments, orders, users, passwords, and the API key are not included in prompt content.

The API key is stored with autoload disabled, can instead be defined with CATEGORY_COMMANDER_OPENAI_API_KEY, and can be deleted from AI Settings. The API-free copy tool does not contact an AI service; data is shared only if the editor pastes the prompt into an external service.

Insights stores local daily aggregate category-link counts. It does not store IP addresses, user IDs, or individual browsing histories.

External service: OpenAI API, https://api.openai.com/v1/responses

Policies: https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement/ and https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy/
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it from the WordPress plugin screen.
  2. Activate Category Commander.
  3. Go to Posts -> Category Commander -> How to Use.
  4. Open Settings and enable only the taxonomies you want to manage. Categories are enabled initially.

Quick start

  1. Open Diagnostics to review local, read-only health checks.
  2. Use Order when you only want to change display order.
  3. Use Category Organizer when category assignments, parent categories, names, or URLs will change. Use Order when only the visible order should change.
  4. Read the affected-post and URL preview, then confirm before applying.
  5. Use the post editor’s Category and tag suggestions panel for optional API suggestions or API-free browser-AI text copy.
  6. Select a Primary Category when a post has several categories.
  7. Use History or Category Organizer history when you need to restore a saved state.

All new rules start as non-blocking warnings. AI suggestions and new terms always remain proposals until an authorized person confirms them.
sections.faq:
Does the plugin change anything during Diagnostics?

No. Diagnostics is a local, read-only report.

Does Category Organizer delete the original category or tag?

No. It replaces or adds assignments as reviewed, saves a restore point, and leaves the source term in place for manual review.

Does a URL impact preview use AI?

No. It is calculated deterministically from current WordPress terms, permalinks, assignments, and primary categories.

Does the AI feature apply changes automatically?

No. Suggestions must be reviewed and confirmed. New categories and tags also require confirmation unless an administrator deliberately changes the policy.

Can I use browser ChatGPT without an API key?

Yes. Copy the complete prompt from the post editor or AI Suggestions screen, paste it into a browser AI, and review the result manually. The plugin does not send copied prompts anywhere.

How many tags are recommended?

The default AI limit and governance warning are five. Existing reusable tags are preferred, and the AI may return fewer when fewer are useful. Administrators can change the limit.

Does Primary Category conflict with an SEO plugin?

No. When Yoast SEO or Rank Math is active, Category Commander uses that plugin’s primary-category value. Otherwise it stores its own value.

Does the plugin modify WordPress core tables?

No. It uses WordPress options, term meta, post meta, and its own aggregate Insights table.

Can it manage tags or custom taxonomies?

Yes. Enable supported public taxonomies in Category Commander -> Settings.

How do I display ordered terms?

Use [category_commander_list], category_commander_get_terms(), or category_commander_terms_list(). The Default preset can also order normal category widgets and blocks when front-end autosort is enabled.
sections.changelog:
1.4.0

  • Removed the developer-only local load-test sample post generator from the distributable plugin.
  • Clarified CSV backup and restore navigation, added direct page focusing, and explained exactly what import changes and preserves.
  • Fixed Japanese CSV text in Excel on macOS and Windows by adding UTF-8 identification and compatible line endings.
  • Added safe import normalization for UTF-8, Excel Unicode, and Japanese Windows CSV files.
  • Prevented parent branches from being placed inside a closed child list during drag and drop.
  • Added a prominent insertion line and “Move here” marker while dragging terms.
  • Fixed parent-category drag placement when child categories are closed, and added a clear insertion marker.
  • Reworked every administration page with grouped navigation, a plain-language purpose, a clear change/no-change notice, and short numbered steps.
  • Added a task-based beginner guide with direct links, a recommended three-step route, a glossary, and safety explanations.
  • Simplified selectors and settings labels, grouped basic and advanced options, and made the API-free browser-AI path prominent.
  • Added Category Organizer for previewed category combinations, selected-post moves, parent changes, names, and URLs.
  • Added deterministic URL and SEO impact previews, redirect CSV, and structural restore history.
  • Added primary categories with Yoast SEO and Rank Math compatibility.
  • Added non-blocking-by-default governance rules and the Taxonomy Health Dashboard.
  • Preserved existing settings and orders; no source term is deleted automatically.

1.3.1

  • Made post-assistant nonce verification and input sanitization explicit for Plugin Check.
  • Removed exclusionary context queries and allowed normal WordPress filters.

1.3.0

  • Added block and Classic Editor category and tag suggestions.
  • Added API-free complete prompt copy, existing-first matching, configurable limits, and confirmation before creating terms.
  • Added GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna choices with migration from older saved picker values.

1.2.1

  • Improved the manual ChatGPT assignment workflow so assignment prompts return to the assignment section instead of the category plan section.
  • Prevented empty post assignment prompts when a selected prompt number does not contain scanned posts.
  • Added clearer post assignment import guidance, valid prompt number guidance, and assignment apply completion status.
  • Marked completed post assignment application clearly so administrators can tell when the workflow is finished.
  • Added stricter validation for imported assignment JSON files.

1.2.0

  • Added optional Category Click Insights for local aggregate category link impressions, clicks, and click-through rate.
  • Added Insights settings for tracked taxonomies, retention, impressions, logged-in user exclusion, search page exclusion, and low-CTR hints.
  • Added an Insights report with period and display-context filters.
  • Added safe cleanup for locally stored Insights data.
  • Added optional AI context so administrator-triggered AI suggestions can include 30-day aggregate category click metrics.
  • Added the category redesign workflow with post scanning, category planning, local post assignments, optional ChatGPT assignment prompts, restore support, safe unused category cleanup, and local sample post generation for testing.

1.1.1

  • Added a manual ChatGPT browser workflow for administrators who do not use the OpenAI API.
  • Added copy/download prompt tools and drag-and-drop JSON result import for manual AI suggestions.
  • Reused the existing safe preview and approval flow for manually imported AI results.
  • Improved AI privacy/help text to distinguish OpenAI API generation from manual ChatGPT browser use.

1.1.0

  • Tested with WordPress 7.0.
  • Added support for tags and public custom taxonomies.
  • Added multiple order presets.
  • Clarified default versus custom preset behavior for widgets, blocks, shortcodes, and developer integrations.
  • Added order history and restore.
  • Added taxonomy diagnostics.
  • Added reset methods.
  • Added shortcode and developer helper functions.
  • Added read-only REST terms endpoint.
  • Added CSV export/import.
  • Added parent/child expand and collapse controls for easier manual ordering.
  • Added an option to show empty child categories in hierarchical category widgets and blocks.
  • Added optional OpenAI-powered order, parent-child structure, and category name suggestions with preview, admin approval, and safe apply flow.
  • Improved AI request progress feedback and detailed troubleshooting output.
  • Added focused AI tasks, editable default prompts, prompt reset controls, structured AI output, saved analysis goals, and more reliable default AI settings.
  • Added optional post title context modes for category name suggestions.
  • Added an option to hide AI reason text for faster, lower-cost category name suggestions.
  • Added safe OpenAI API key deletion from AI Settings.
  • Improved privacy disclosures and external service documentation.
  • Improved contextual Help tabs for AI settings, AI suggestions, front-end display behavior, privacy, shortcodes, and common WordPress terms.
  • Improved security checks, sanitization, escaping, and capability filters.

1.0.5

  • Remove manual text-domain loading code to align with WordPress.org Plugin Check guidance.
  • Improve keyboard reordering usability: click-to-select state with visible highlight, then Alt (Option on Mac) + Up/Down to move.

1.0.4

  • Improve i18n/l10n coverage for admin and REST user-facing messages.
  • Add proper textdomain loading on plugins_loaded.
  • Add/update translation template in languages/category-commander.pot.

1.0.3

  • Add compatibility notice and conflict guidance on the admin page.
  • Load text domain for translations.

1.0.2

  • Improve ordering stability when other plugins modify category queries.

1.0.1

  • Initial release.
